newsitem.title: USA: Citicorp CEO sees Q1 EPS meeting forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Citicorp CEO sees Q1 EPS meeting forecasts.

text.p: Citicorp chief executive John Reed told shareholders on Wednesday that first-quarter profits would meet Wall Street forecasts, saying "nothing special" was likely to appear in the report due next Tuesday.

Reed gave no figures at Citicorp's annual meeting, but analysts polled by I/B/E/S are forecasting the global banking group will report share profits between $1.75 and $2.07. I/B/E/S has a mean estimate of $1.99, while the First Call mean estimate is $2.00, versus $1.75 in last year's first quarter.
"The quarter should be pretty much in line with expectations," Reed said. "There is nothing special in it I can share with you."
Reed did not discuss sector performance in the three months ended March 31, but banking analysts worry that U.S. credit-card losses at Citicorp could have enlarged from late 1996.

In last year's fourth quarter, Citicorp reported that "credit costs" were 5.45 percent of average managed loans, up from 5.11 percent in the previous quarter. The rate was only 3.89 percent in the fourth quarter of 1995.
Reed, who is also chairman, said 1997 and 1998 would be more difficult years for Citicorp than 1996, "only because last year was so benign."
